$comment: AI-readiness assessment matrix derived from Table 11 of González-Espinoza et al. (2026). 7 Bridge2AI dimensions × 3 readiness levels (L1/L2/L3 ↔ DRL bands C/B/A). Cumulative semantics: Pathway A requires every L1 criterion; Pathway B requires every L1 + L2; Pathway C requires every L1 + L2 + L3. The Croissant descriptor lives at L2 but is marked recommended at L1 to keep upgrades frictionless. Pathway C sub-domain overlays live in pathways.json, not here — they may target any dimension, and a sub-domain may also reword a criterion below via 'label_overrides' (wording only; id, evidence_type, and pathway membership are never changed). All five schema files move in lockstep from 0.3.0; 1.0.0 is cut when the criterion ids are considered stable.

criteria.label: Persistent identifier assigned (DOI, ARK, or repository accession)
criteria.remediation: Mint a DOI via Zenodo, DataCite, or your institutional repository before publishing. The identifier must resolve to a landing page, not directly to a file.

criteria.label: Landing page URL with human-readable metadata
criteria.remediation: Most repositories generate a landing page automatically when you mint a DOI. Confirm the page is publicly resolvable.

criteria.label: Metadata exposed in a machine-readable format (DataCite, schema.org/Dataset, or JSON-LD)
criteria.remediation: Confirm the landing page emits DataCite metadata or schema.org/Dataset JSON-LD. Most generalist repositories do this by default.

criteria.label: Access protocol documented (open download, request form, or controlled-access process)
criteria.remediation: State explicitly how a user obtains the data: open download, registration, DUA, or DAC review.

criteria.label: Explicit, machine-readable license
criteria.remediation: Pick a Creative Commons or Open Data Commons license. 'No license' defaults to all-rights-reserved and blocks reuse.

criteria.label: Croissant 1.0 descriptor present and validates against the MLCommons schema
criteria.remediation: Use the in-app Croissant generator. Including a descriptor at L1 makes the dataset directly ML-loadable today and trivially upgradable to L2.

criteria.label: Variable terms drawn from recognised controlled vocabularies where applicable
criteria.remediation: Map clinical fields to LOINC/SNOMED, units to UCUM, climate vars to CF, etc. Document the mapping in the Croissant descriptor.

criteria.label: Links to related datasets, schemas, or ontologies (qualified references)
criteria.remediation: Include `isVersionOf`, `isPartOf`, `references`, or schema.org/sameAs links so machines can navigate between related artefacts.

criteria.label: Croissant descriptor includes Responsible-AI annotations (intended use, known limitations, sensitive attributes)
criteria.collection_hint: While you are deciding what the data is for, write the one-line intended use and the uses you would object to. Both are easier to state before there are results to defend.
criteria.remediation: Populate the Croissant `rai:` namespace fields. The in-app generator surfaces them when Pathway C is selected.

criteria.label: Versioned release with concept-level and version-level identifiers; immutable per version
criteria.collection_hint: Fix the version string for this cut of the data, and note what would make you cut the next one.
criteria.remediation: Use a repository that mints both a concept DOI (resolves to latest) and version-specific DOIs (Zenodo and DataCite both support this).

criteria.label: Deposition repository selected with appropriate access tier
criteria.collection_hint: Pick the target repository early and read its submission requirements: some constrain formats, consent wording, or file layout in ways that are cheap to satisfy before collection and expensive after.
criteria.remediation: The options are scoped to your pathway and, in Pathway C, to your sub-domain — a domain repository is preferred over a generalist one, and any target recommended for your sub-domain is listed first. Record the repository you will deposit in and the access tier it will carry (open, registered, restricted, controlled, or embargoed). If the right repository is not listed, use Custom.

criteria.label: Original sources of the data described in prose (instruments, registries, surveys, or upstream datasets)
criteria.remediation: Add a 'Sources' section to the README or datasheet listing every upstream source and how it was obtained.

criteria.label: When and where the data was collected (time window, geography or instrument)
criteria.remediation: State the inclusive collection dates and any geographic/cohort constraints. This is what downstream users need to judge fit.

criteria.label: Every curation and transformation step listed in prose (cleaning, harmonisation, derivation rules)
criteria.remediation: List each step with inputs, outputs, and rationale. The PROV-O generator produces a structured version of this — write the prose first, encode it second.

criteria.label: Software, scripts, and library versions used to produce the released dataset
criteria.remediation: Capture interpreter version, library pins (requirements.txt or environment.yml), and a Git commit hash for in-house code.

criteria.label: PROV-O JSON-LD record accompanies the released dataset
criteria.collection_hint: Keep the run log the record is built from: for every processing step, its inputs, its outputs, and when it ran.
criteria.remediation: Use the in-app PROV-O generator for short pipelines, or export from CWL / Snakemake / Nextflow / Galaxy for long ones.

criteria.label: PROV record contains an Entity per dataset version and per declared variable
criteria.collection_hint: List every variable you will release; for derived ones, note which variables they were computed from.
criteria.remediation: Variable-level Entities enable feature-lineage queries downstream. The in-app generator emits one Entity per variable when the variable list is populated.

criteria.label: PROV record contains an Activity per curation/transformation step, with parameters and software version
criteria.collection_hint: At run time, record the parameters used and the exact software version. Version numbers are the first thing to become unrecoverable.
criteria.remediation: Each Activity records `prov:used` (inputs), `prov:wasGeneratedBy` (outputs), parameters, and the software Agent that ran it.

criteria.label: Agents declared with CRediT-style roles drawn from Table 12
criteria.collection_hint: Note who ran each step, by ORCID, and in what role.
criteria.remediation: Name a data steward, domain expert, data engineer, ML practitioner, and governance officer — even if the same person holds multiple roles in a small team.

criteria.label: Schema declared: types, units, and allowed values per variable
criteria.remediation: Ship a data dictionary (CSV, Markdown, or DDI XML) listing every variable with its type, units, and value set.

criteria.label: Total record count and basic shape (rows × columns, or equivalent)
criteria.remediation: One sentence in the README. Trivial to provide and always missed.

criteria.label: Missingness rates per variable
criteria.remediation: Report % missing per variable. Default missingness handling encodes fairness properties — disclose what was applied.

criteria.label: Summary statistics per variable (numeric: min/max/mean/std; categorical: value counts)
criteria.remediation: A one-page summary or a Great-Expectations / Pandera profiling report. Include in the documentation bundle.

criteria.label: Known errors and their treatment (corrected, flagged, dropped, or left in)
criteria.remediation: Explicit disclosure beats silent correction. List known issues even if you chose not to fix them.

criteria.label: Class balance for classification targets (where applicable; mark N/A otherwise)
criteria.remediation: Report counts per class. Heavy imbalance affects evaluation metrics — surfacing it lets reviewers judge fit.

criteria.label: Bias audit: representation parity across protected attributes and curation-induced skew
criteria.collection_hint: Record the attributes you will need to audit representation on — site, instrument, batch, demographic group — as columns, not as prose. You cannot audit what was never captured.
criteria.remediation: Use Aequitas, Fairlearn, or an equivalent tool. Compare distributions before and after curation to detect introduced skew, not just released-state parity.

criteria.label: Temporal, geographic, demographic, and modality coverage analysis
criteria.collection_hint: Note the span the data actually covers: dates, sites, instruments, populations, modalities. Also note what you intended to cover and did not.
criteria.remediation: List subgroups represented and subgroups missing. Coverage gaps constrain valid downstream uses.

criteria.label: Intended uses and out-of-scope uses declared explicitly
criteria.collection_hint: Write down the question this data was collected to answer. That sentence becomes the intended-use statement.
criteria.remediation: State both: tasks the dataset should support, and tasks it should not (e.g., 'not for clinical decision support').

criteria.label: Known selection effects, measurement error, and confounders documented
criteria.collection_hint: Keep a running note of anything that went wrong or changed mid-stream: a failed batch, a recalibration, an amended protocol, a site that dropped out.
criteria.remediation: Healthcare-utilisation proxies, exclusion windows, instrument quirks — name them. Downstream users need them to judge transferability.

criteria.label: Consent basis recorded (or explicit non-applicability)
criteria.remediation: Document what consent covers — including 'not applicable' for non-human-subjects or already-public data.

criteria.label: Direct identifiers removed or transformed
criteria.remediation: Names, contact details, MRNs, exact addresses, exact dates of service. Indirect identifiers come at L2.

criteria.label: De-identification method recorded (which standard, which parameters)
criteria.remediation: 'Stripped names' is not a method. Record HIPAA Safe Harbor / Expert Determination / k-anonymity (with k) / differential privacy (with ε), etc.

criteria.label: Ethics oversight documented as metadata (approving body, protocol ID, approval date, scope of permitted use, expiry/renewal status)
criteria.collection_hint: Record the approving body, protocol number, and approval date when approval is granted, not when you write the paper.
criteria.remediation: The review itself happens before/during acquisition. What travels with the dataset at L3 is structured evidence of that review — that is the L3 requirement.

criteria.label: Tiered access governance in place (open / registered / restricted / controlled / embargoed)
criteria.collection_hint: Decide before collection who will be allowed access and under what conditions — consent wording usually has to match the access tier you intend.
criteria.remediation: Match the access tier to the sensitivity of the data and the consent basis recorded at L1.

criteria.label: Data-use agreement template referenced if access is restricted or controlled (mark N/A for open access)
criteria.collection_hint: If access will be restricted, note which data-use agreement applies, or that one still has to be drafted.
criteria.remediation: Link to the DUA template the requester signs. Repositories like PhysioNet ship one; institutional Dataverse instances often do too.

criteria.label: Whether secondary use is permitted, and under what constraints
criteria.collection_hint: Record what the consent or licence actually permits beyond this study, in the words the document uses.
criteria.remediation: Bound by what consent basis at L1 supports. Be explicit — silence here defaults reviewers to 'not permitted'.

criteria.label: Every variable has a human-readable definition
criteria.remediation: A column name is not a definition. Each variable needs a sentence explaining what it measures and how.

criteria.label: Units recorded for every measured variable
criteria.remediation: Use UCUM where applicable. Untyped numerics are a frequent cause of merge errors across cohorts.

criteria.label: Derived variables traceable to source variable(s) and the operation that produced them
criteria.remediation: BMI = mass / height² is a source-and-operation. Record both, not just the derived value.

criteria.label: Encodings documented (one-hot, normalisation, tokenisation, vocabulary mappings)
criteria.remediation: If the released artefact is post-encoding, ship the encoder configuration / tokenizer alongside it.

criteria.label: Feature lineage preserved end-to-end via the PROV record
criteria.collection_hint: As you create each derived variable, note its source variables and the operation that produced it.
criteria.remediation: Every released feature can be reconstructed from raw inputs by following the PROV record's `wasDerivedFrom` chain.

criteria.label: Released alongside or linkable to a model card (when models trained on this data exist)
criteria.collection_hint: If a model will be trained on this data, note where its model card will live.
criteria.remediation: Triangular linkage from Figure 8: dataset DOI ↔ model DOI/HF ID ↔ results DOI. Link bidirectionally so each artefact resolves to the others.

criteria.label: Released in an open, non-proprietary format
criteria.remediation: Parquet / CSV for tabular; HDF5 / NetCDF / Zarr for arrays; DICOM / NIfTI for imaging. Avoid Excel, SAS, or vendor formats as the canonical release.

criteria.label: Total size and per-file size reported
criteria.remediation: One line in the README. Lets downstream users plan downloads and storage.

criteria.label: Long-term access plan (institutional commitment, repository SLA, or migration strategy)
criteria.remediation: Use a repository with an institutional commitment (Zenodo's CERN backing, institutional Dataverse, etc.). 'Hosted on a personal server' is not a long-term plan.

criteria.label: At least one data-centric efficiency intervention applied (curation / distillation / active learning / curriculum)
criteria.collection_hint: If you curate, distil, or subsample before release, record what you removed and why. That decision is invisible in the released file.
criteria.remediation: Document which intervention was applied and the metric it improved (records removed, accuracy at matched compute, etc.).

criteria.label: Compute cost of producing this release reported (compute hours, hardware type, energy or estimated emissions)
criteria.collection_hint: Note the compute this release consumed as you go: core-hours or instance-hours, the machine, and how many runs. Schedulers report it, and queue history rolls over.
criteria.remediation: Bind these figures to the same release bundle as the datasheet and PROV record. Without disclosure, efficiency claims are unverifiable.

criteria.label: Loadable in a standard scientific-computing environment (pandas, numpy, R, or domain-equivalent)
criteria.remediation: If a reviewer can't `pd.read_parquet(path)` or its domain equivalent, the format is wrong.

criteria.label: Codebook or data dictionary shipped alongside the data
criteria.remediation: Variable name, type, units, value set, and a one-sentence description per field. Markdown, CSV, or DDI all work.

criteria.label: Field values map to recognised controlled vocabularies where applicable (LOINC / SNOMED / UCUM / CF / ICD-10 / etc.)
criteria.remediation: Without controlled vocabularies, two correctly-documented datasets still cannot be aligned. Record the vocabulary version, not just its name.

criteria.label: Schemas referenced as linked external schemas (DDI, BIDS, CF-conventions, schema.org)
criteria.remediation: Reference the schema by URL inside the Croissant descriptor's `conformsTo` field.

criteria.label: Croissant descriptor enables direct load into ML frameworks without custom parsing
criteria.collection_hint: As files are produced, list them and the columns inside them, with types and units.
criteria.remediation: Verify with `mlcroissant` reference library: a four-line load (see Code Block 2 in the source paper) should yield records.

criteria.label: Example load snippet provided (TensorFlow Datasets, Hugging Face, or PyTorch DataLoader)
criteria.collection_hint: Keep the few lines you yourself used to load the data. That is the snippet.
criteria.remediation: Five lines of Python in the README that load the dataset and print one record. Removes ambiguity that prose cannot.
